subject: Polity
description: Attorney General, CAG, Advocate General, PMO

questions.stem: The Attorney General for India is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Art 76 — the Attorney General for India is appointed by the President and holds office during the pleasure of the President. Eligibility — same as for a Supreme Court judge. The AG is the highest law officer of the Union. Solicitor General and Additional Solicitors General assist the AG. Each state has an Advocate General (Art 165) appointed by the Governor.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India is appointed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Art 148 establishes the office of the CAG. Appointed by the President; holds office for 6 years or till the age of 65, whichever is earlier. Removable only in the manner of a Supreme Court judge. B. R. Ambedkar called the CAG 'the most important officer of the Constitution'. Submits three audit reports — Union, state, PSUs — to the President / Governor, who lays them before the Legislature.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Advocate General of a state is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Art 165 — the Advocate General is the highest law officer of a state, appointed by the Governor. Holds office during the pleasure of the Governor. Eligibility — qualified to be a High Court judge. Right of audience in any court in the state and right to take part in the proceedings of the state legislature (though not to vote). Parallel — Attorney General (for India) under Art 76.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Finance Commission of India is constituted every:
questions.explanation: Art 280 — the Finance Commission is constituted every 5 years (or earlier) by the President. Its mandate — recommending the devolution of taxes between the Union and the states and amongst the states, grants-in-aid, and other fiscal matters. The current 16th FC (Chairman Arvind Panagariya) will submit recommendations for 2026-31. The 15th FC's awards (N. K. Singh) cover 2021-26. or earlier if needed.

options.option_text: An executive body, not created by the Constitution
A statutory body created by Parliament

questions.explanation: The PMO is an executive office that evolved from the PM's Secretariat; it is not a creation of the Constitution. Its head — the Principal Secretary to the PM (IAS officer). Handles briefs for the PM, coordinates inter-ministerial work, maintains the PM's official correspondence. Unlike the Cabinet Secretariat (serves the entire Cabinet) the PMO works directly for the PM.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) is appointed by the:
questions.explanation: Art 316 — the Chairman and members of UPSC are appointed by the President. Hold office for 6 years or till the age of 65, whichever is earlier. UPSC (Art 315) conducts the civil-services exam (IAS, IPS, IFS etc.), CDS, NDA and advises on recruitment rules and service matters. State PSC — appointed by the Governor; hold office till age 62.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Comptroller and Auditor General holds office for a term of:
questions.explanation: CAG — 6-year term or up to age 65, whichever is earlier. Salary and conditions of service charged on the Consolidated Fund (not subject to parliamentary vote — guaranteeing independence). Can be removed only in the same manner as a Supreme Court judge (proved misbehaviour / incapacity, two-thirds special majority). Once retired, barred from further office under Union / state governments.
